title: One unplaceable-reference rule replaces six reference lints
summary: This change collapses six separate reference lints (bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name, undefined-name-at-start) into a single `unplaceable-reference` rule backed by a new candidate-and-placement engine in `crates/osf/src/lints/writing/reference.rs`. The engine extracts four kinds of candidate (number, phrase, time, name) from a paragraph, then decides whether the paragraph itself places each one — a link, a bracketed description, a named repository, a file path, an absolute date, a known name, or a definer sentence. Findings carry an `Evidence` value, and `osf-lint-core::resolve` now takes that evidence: statistical evidence (a guessed name, a quoted term) always resolves to Warning/Advise in every context, so a weak guess can never refuse a reply at the stop hook. A new fixture corpus and two end-to-end test files measure precision and recall and prove the rule fires at the stop hook, the commit-message check and the prompt hook.

lanes.label: Entry points
lanes.subtitle: hooks, CLI, scan
lanes.summary: The surfaces that hand text to the writing lint: the stop hook, the commit-message check, the prompt hook and the scan command.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf-lint-core
lanes.summary: Shared rule machinery: the class/group/context matrix that turns a finding into a level and a remediation.

lanes.label: Writing lints
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing
lanes.summary: The writing rule set, including the new candidate-and-placement engine and the rule metadata table.

lanes.label: Fixtures and tests
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests
lanes.summary: The unplaceable fixture corpus and the end-to-end tests that measure and checkpoint the new rule.

nodes.label: Stop hook
nodes.subtitle: hook.rs stop_with_input
nodes.summary: Reads the assistant's last message from stdin and decides whether to refuse the turn. A refusal now depends on the resolved level of each finding, so a statistical-evidence finding can no longer refuse on its own.

nodes.label: Commit-message check
nodes.subtitle: osf lint writing --context commit
nodes.summary: Lints a commit message file. The new rule runs here in commit context, where a relative time is a candidate and a bare word-and-number label fails the check.

nodes.label: Prompt hook
nodes.subtitle: hook prompt reminder
nodes.summary: Prints the reminder shown on every prompt. It must never name a retired rule id, which the new checkpoint test asserts.

nodes.label: Scan command
nodes.subtitle: scan/mod.rs resolve_and_explain
nodes.summary: Resolves each scan finding's level and remediation. It now passes the finding's own evidence into the shared resolver.

nodes.label: resolve()
nodes.subtitle: class, group, context, exception, evidence
nodes.summary: The one place a finding's level and remediation are decided. A new first branch returns Warning/Advise for statistical evidence before any class, group, context or exception is consulted.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.subtitle: Deterministic | Statistical
nodes.summary: The finding's own evidence, carried on every Finding. Statistical means the rule guessed, so the resolver treats it as advisory everywhere.

nodes.label: lint_writing()
nodes.subtitle: writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Runs the writing rule set over a document and then applies context. It now calls the new unplaceable_reference rule and passes each finding's evidence into rule metadata resolution.

nodes.label: unplaceable_reference()
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs
nodes.summary: The new rule. Gathers candidates per paragraph, picks one paragraph to report each repeated name from, and emits one finding per candidate the paragraph does not place.

nodes.label: reference.rs
nodes.subtitle: candidates, Candidate, Kind
nodes.summary: The candidate engine: extracts Number, Phrase, Time and Name candidates from a paragraph, masks quoted and backticked spans, and keeps the longest candidate per kind when two overlap.

nodes.label: is_placed()
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs
nodes.summary: Decides whether the paragraph itself places a candidate: a link, a bracketed description, a named repository, a file path, an absolute date, a known name, or a definer sentence.

nodes.label: RULE_META
nodes.subtitle: writing/meta.rs
nodes.summary: The rule metadata table. It gains the unplaceable-reference entry and its resolve() now takes the finding's evidence.

nodes.label: KnownNames
nodes.subtitle: names.rs BUILT_IN, is_generic_word
nodes.summary: The built-in name list gains frameworks, design systems and model tiers (React, Vite, Tauri, Sonnet, Opus, Haiku, RFC). A new is_generic_word lets the number exclusion tell a real name from a generic label word such as Phase.

nodes.label: unplaceable fixtures
nodes.subtitle: 67 markdown cases
nodes.summary: A corpus of placeable and unplaceable paragraphs, each with an osf-unplaceable header naming its kind, target and reason. It is the ground truth the measure test scores against.

nodes.label: unplaceable_measure.rs
nodes.subtitle: precision and recall
nodes.summary: Scores the rule against the fixture corpus per kind and in total, requiring perfect precision and recall and no stray findings.

nodes.label: unplaceable_checkpoints.rs
nodes.subtitle: end-to-end binary checks
nodes.summary: Runs the compiled osf binary at the stop hook, the commit-message check and the prompt hook to prove the rule fires where it should and never names a retired rule id.

edges.label: last assistant message
edges.summary: The stop hook lints the reply text before deciding whether to refuse the turn.

edges.label: commit message
edges.summary: The commit-message check lints the message file in commit context.

edges.label: evidence
edges.summary: The scan command now passes each finding's evidence into the shared resolver.

edges.label: doc, known, cfg, context
edges.summary: The new rule is wired into the writing rule set, running beside the older reference rules until they are retired.

edges.label: candidates(unit, cfg, known, context, run_counts)
edges.summary: The rule asks the engine for every candidate in a paragraph, then judges placement itself.

edges.label: is_placed(...)
edges.summary: Each candidate is tested against the paragraph's own text for a placement.

edges.label: resolve(context, evidence)
edges.summary: Context application now passes the finding's evidence into rule metadata resolution.

edges.label: class, group, context, exception, evidence
edges.summary: Rule metadata forwards the evidence to the shared resolver.

edges.label: Evidence::Statistical
edges.summary: A statistical finding short-circuits to Warning/Advise before any other input is read.

edges.label: known.contains, is_generic_word
edges.summary: The engine consults the known-names list to exclude a number after a real name, and the generic-word check to keep a number after a label word such as Phase.

edges.label: 67 cases
edges.summary: The measure test reads every fixture header and scores the rule's findings against the declared target.

edges.label: hook stop over stdin
edges.summary: The checkpoint test drives the real binary's stop hook with a JSON event on stdin.
